lines.text: Many learners say: She explained me the problem.
Better: She explained the problem to me.
Say the thing first. Then to me.
He explained the rule to me!

data.right: She explained the problem to me.
data.why: Say the thing first. Then to me.

options: He explained the rule to me.

native.tip: En français, on dit « il m’a expliqué le problème ». En anglais, la chose vient d’abord, puis “to me”.
native.caption: Vous dites “She explained me the problem.” ? Avec “explain”, on place d’abord la chose, puis “to” et la personne. Dites plutôt “She explained the problem to me.” — écoutez Ama et répétez avec elle ! Plus d’exercices dans l’appli Lexkite.
native.comment: Réponse : “She explained the problem to me.” — Avec “explain”, on place d’abord la chose, puis “to” et la personne. Testez d’autres pièges avec un quiz gratuit : {link}

en.tip: It sounds natural to say “explain me”, but English puts the thing first, then “to me”.
en.caption: Do you say this? “She explained me the problem.” With “explain”, put the thing first, then “to” and the person. Say “She explained the problem to me.” Listen to Ama and repeat with her! More exercises in the Lexkite app.
